data.name: Kassander
data.gender_notes: Kassander is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'kassanos', meaning 'executor of a man's will'. In Greek mythology, Kassander was a Macedonian nobleman who became the regent for his nephew, Alexander IV, and later seized the throne for himself. The name Kassander carries the meaning “Executor of a man's will” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Kassander usually hope their child will grow to embody executor of a man's will and live with faith, good character and purpose.

The name Kassander is also associated with the idea of leadership and authority, and is often given to children born into families of high social status. In terms of personality traits, individuals with the name Kassander are often seen as confident, charismatic, and strong-willed, with a strong sense of loyalty and duty. In modern usage, the name Kassander is not as commonly given as it once was, but it still maintains a strong presence in Christian cultures around the world.
